sentences.text: 2 This petition is filed by the petitioner/de-facto complainant under Section 407 of Cr.P.C for transferring the case in CC.No.25273/2019 from 39th ACMM Bangalore to JMFC, Udupi to try and dispose off the criminal case registered in Crime No.10/2019 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with 34 or IPC.

2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioner, learned HCGP for the respondent Nos.1 and 2/State and learned counsel for respondent Nos.3 to 6.
3.
The case of the petitioner is that she had married to respondent No. 3 at Udupi.

Later, she came and stayed with her husband at the matrimonial home at Gayatri Nagar, Bangalore and during those days, the respondent Nos.3 to 6 said to have harassed and assaulted her physically and mentally by demanding dowry etc.,
Therefore, she went back to the matrimonial home at Udupi and filed a complaint before the Superintendent of Police.

Inturn, the complaint has been NC:
2023:KHC:21593 forwarded to the Women Police Station, Udupi and a case was registered by the Udupi police in Crime No.10/2019.
During the investigation, the police made a requisition to the JMFC, Udupi for transferring the investigation to Bangalore on the point of jurisdiction vide request dated 13.3.2019.
In pursuance of the requisition, the Magistrate permitted the police to transfer the case.

Accordingly, the Subramanya Nagar police, Bengaluru received the transfer complaint and registered the case in Crime No.66/2019 for the same offences and took up the investigation and filed the charge sheet.
Now the same is pending before the 39th ACMM Bengaluru and the petitioner being the de-facto complainant filed this petition for transfer, on the ground that complaint came to be filed at Udupi.

The parents of the petitioner are in Udupi, the marriage took place in Udupi, therefore, it is very difficult for her to attend the Court at Bangalore for giving evidence as her parents also are required to travel from Udupi to Bangalore, which may cause inconvenience and great hardship.
Therefore, prayed for transferring the case.
Per contra, learned counsel for respondent Nos.3 to 6 objected the petition mainly on the ground the entire incident as per the complaint took place at Subramanya Nagar police limit.
Therefore, the police rightly transferred the investigation to Bangalore and filed charge sheet.
Now there are 4 accused persons who are facing the trial.

Therefore, if these 4 accused persons have to travel to Udupi on each and every date of hearing, it may cause more hardship and inconvenience for them to attend the courts for every dates of hearing till conclusion of the trial.
Therefore, the respondent Nos.3 to 6 are having more inconvenience to attend the court than the petitioner.

That apart, the learned counsel also submits, the petitioner already filed petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C for quashing the order of permitting the police to transfer the investigation, which was dismissed by the co-ordinate bench of this Court.
Therefore, prayed for dismissing the petition.
5. Learned HCGP also submitted that both the courts have the jurisdiction to try the offences.

sentences.text: 3 6. Having heard the arguments and perused the records, of course, the marriage was held at Udupi.

The parents of the complainant also are from Udupi, but immediately after the marriage the complainant stayed with the accused the matrimonial house at Gayatri Nagar, Bangalore, which is within the jurisdiction of Subramanyanagar police station, Bengaluru.

The complaint itself reveals that after one week of staying with the accused, the accused persons had assaulted the complainant physically and mentally for dowry etc., Until the entire episode of harassment regarding offence attracting section 498A of IPC, had occurred at Bengaluru.
Of course, the complainant can also file the complaint before the Udupi police, which was her last resident, i.e, her parent's house.

However,
the accused persons in order to travel from Bangalore to Udupi, which is more than 400 kilometres,
they may have to travel frequently to attend the case.
Also, they may require 3 days to attend the case on every hearing date, till the conclusion of the trial they have to appear before the trial court.
On the other hand, the presence of the complainant and her parents may be required for the trial court, only for giving evidence in the trial court.

The petitioner and the parents may come to NC:
2023:KHC:21593 the court only for the purpose of giving evidence or cross examination that may take one or two dates of hearing and may not be required to attend continuously and on every dates of hearing at Bangalore.
By considering the same, it is more inconvenient which will be caused to respondent Nos.3 to 6.

That apart, the coordinate bench of this Court already dismissed the petition under section 482 of Cr.P.C where the police made request for transferring the investigation had been challenged and it was dismissed by the coordinate bench of this Court, it is nothing but a second round of litigation by the petitioner.

7. However, the petitioner and her parents may be required to attend the Court and to meet the ends of justice, the trial court may grant some Travel Allowance and Dearness Allowance to the witnesses otherwise the witness Bata may be granted to them for attending the court during the trial.

Therefore, the petitioner will not have any inconvenience or hardship which may be caused to her for attending court only for the purpose of evidence or else more inconvenience or hardship will be caused to the accused persons i.e, respondent NC: 2023:KHC:21593 Nos.3 to 6.
Therefore, I am of the view, petition is devoid of merits.
Accordingly, petition is dismissed.

The trial court can impose cost of actual travelling expenses to the petitioner and her parents when they appear for the trial for giving evidence, at the cost of respondent No. 3 to 6.
Sd/-
